summary: Icon component — a design-token-driven wrapper around a single glyph. (Package docs; Coin has no designer guide for Icon.)

examples.purpose: A registry icon resolved through modes.

props.name: iconName
props.description: Built-in icon name from the registry, in the `ic_something` format (e.g. `'ic_card'`, `'ic_scan_qr_code'`). When omitted and no `source` or `children` slot is supplied, defaults to `'ic_card'` to match the Figma design's default glyph.

props.name: source
props.description: Unified fallback source rendered when `iconName` is missing or not in the registry. Accepts a remote URI, an inline SVG XML string, a `require()` asset, an SVG React component, or an already-rendered element. The media is tinted with the mode-resolved icon color so it follows design tokens just like a built-in icon. See {@link UnifiedSource}.

props.name: children
props.description: Icon slot. Render any node here (another `Icon`, a custom SVG component, etc.) and it takes precedence over `iconName`/`source`. `modes` cascade into the slotted children automatically.

props.name: color
props.description: Override the mode-resolved icon color. When omitted the value comes from the `icon/color` design token.

props.name: size
props.description: Override the mode-resolved icon size (in px). When omitted the value comes from the `icon/size` design token.

props.name: ...AccessibilityProps
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: AppearanceBrand
modes.description: A token collection Icon reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.
